alabama.labor_agency_name: Alabama Department of Workforce (formerly Alabama Department of Labor)
alabama.state_note: Alabama's Retirement Systems of Alabama provides defined-benefit pensions for state employees, teachers, and other public employees, with benefits vesting after 10 years of service.

alaska.labor_agency_name: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development — Wage and Hour Administration
alaska.ag_name: Alaska Attorney General — Consumer Protection Unit
alaska.state_note: Alaska's Public Employees' Retirement System offers pension and retiree insurance benefits; workers hired before July 1, 2006 are in its defined-benefit plan.

arizona.labor_agency_name: Industrial Commission of Arizona — Labor Department
arizona.ag_name: Arizona Attorney General's Office — Consumer Information and Complaints
arizona.state_note: Arizona's State Retirement System provides a lifetime defined-benefit pension, plus long-term disability and retiree health benefits, to state and local public employees.

arkansas.labor_agency_name: Arkansas Department of Labor and Licensing — Labor Standards Division
arkansas.ag_name: Arkansas Attorney General — Consumer Protection Division
arkansas.state_note: Arkansas's Public Employees Retirement System is a defined-benefit pension plan covering state, county, and participating municipal and school employees.

california.labor_agency_name: California Labor Commissioner's Office (Division of Labor Standards Enforcement)
california.ag_name: California Attorney General — Public Inquiry Unit
california.state_note: California's CalSavers program requires employers without a retirement plan to offer workers automatic enrollment in a portable Roth IRA.

colorado.labor_agency_name: Colorado Department of Labor and Employment — Division of Labor Standards and Statistics
colorado.ag_name: Colorado Attorney General — Stop Fraud Colorado
colorado.state_note: Colorado's Public Employees' Retirement Association provides a lifetime defined-benefit pension to state, school, and many local government employees.

connecticut.labor_agency_name: Connecticut Department of Labor — Wage and Workplace Standards Division
connecticut.ag_name: Connecticut Office of the Attorney General
connecticut.state_note: Connecticut's MyCTSavings program requires employers with five or more workers and no retirement plan to enroll employees in an automatic Roth IRA.

delaware.labor_agency_name: Delaware Department of Labor — Office of Wage & Hour Enforcement
delaware.ag_name: Delaware Department of Justice — Consumer Protection Unit
delaware.state_note: Delaware's Public Employees' Retirement System provides pensions to state employees, with unreduced benefits after 30 years of service at any age.

florida.ag_name: Florida Attorney General — Office of Citizen Services
florida.state_note: Florida's Retirement System offers public employees a choice between a defined-benefit Pension Plan and a defined-contribution Investment Plan.

georgia.ag_name: Georgia Attorney General — Consumer Protection Division
georgia.state_note: Georgia's Employees' Retirement System provides a defined-benefit pension to state employees, vesting after 10 years of creditable service.

hawaii.labor_agency_name: Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Wage Standards Division
hawaii.ag_name: Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Office of Consumer Protection (handles consumer complaints for the Attorney General)
hawaii.state_note: Hawaii's Employees' Retirement System provides defined-benefit pensions to state and county employees, including teachers, police, and firefighters.

idaho.ag_name: Idaho Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
idaho.state_note: Idaho's Public Employee Retirement System (PERSI) provides a defined-benefit Base Plan paying public employees a lifetime monthly pension to supplement Social Security.

illinois.ag_name: Illinois Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
illinois.state_note: Illinois' State Employees' Retirement System (SERS) provides state employees a lifetime pension based on final average compensation and service, exempt from Illinois income tax.

indiana.labor_agency_name: Indiana Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
indiana.ag_name: Indiana Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
indiana.state_note: Indiana's Public Employees' Retirement Fund (PERF) Hybrid plan combines a defined-benefit pension with a 401(a) account for state and local public employees.

iowa.labor_agency_name: Iowa Division of Labor, Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing (DIAL)
iowa.ag_name: Iowa Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
iowa.state_note: IPERS, created in 1953, is Iowa's largest public retirement plan, paying guaranteed lifetime defined benefits to public employees.

kansas.labor_agency_name: Kansas Department of Labor, Office of Employment Standards
kansas.state_note: KPERS delivers retirement, disability, and survivor benefits to Kansas public employees, police and firefighters, and judges.

kentucky.labor_agency_name: Kentucky Education and Labor Cabinet, Division of Wages and Hours
kentucky.ag_name: Kentucky Attorney General, Office of Consumer Protection
kentucky.state_note: Kentucky's Public Pensions Authority runs KERS, CERS, and SPRS defined-benefit plans for most state, county, and state police employees.

louisiana.ag_name: Louisiana Attorney General, Consumer Protection Section
louisiana.state_note: LASERS is a defined-benefit plan providing retirement, survivor, and disability benefits to Louisiana state employees.

maine.labor_agency_name: Maine Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Standards, Wage and Hour Division
maine.ag_name: Maine Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
maine.state_note: MainePERS has provided defined-benefit pensions since 1942 to teachers and state, county, and municipal employees; members vest after five years.

maryland.labor_agency_name: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Labor and Industry, Employment Standards Service
maryland.ag_name: Maryland Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
maryland.state_note: Maryland's State Retirement and Pension System administers defined-benefit retirement, disability, and survivor benefits for over 420,000 members.

massachusetts.labor_agency_name: Massachusetts Attorney General, Fair Labor Division
massachusetts.ag_name: Massachusetts Attorney General, Consumer Advocacy & Response Division
massachusetts.state_note: The Massachusetts State Retirement Board runs the State Employees' Retirement System, a defined benefit pension under state law for state employees and certain other public workers.

michigan.labor_agency_name: Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity, Wage and Hour Division
michigan.ag_name: Michigan Department of Attorney General, Consumer Protection Team
michigan.state_note: Michigan's Office of Retirement Services runs the State Employees' Retirement System, a defined benefit pension for state workers hired before March 31, 1997, plus a defined contribution plan for later hires.

minnesota.labor_agency_name: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry, Labor Standards Division
minnesota.ag_name: Minnesota Attorney General, Consumer Action Division
minnesota.state_note: The Minnesota State Retirement System manages defined benefit pension funds covering state employees, State Patrol, corrections workers, judges, and legislators.

mississippi.ag_name: Mississippi Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
mississippi.state_note: Mississippi's Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) is a defined benefit plan providing lifetime pensions to eligible state and local public employees.

missouri.labor_agency_name: Missouri Department of Labor and Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards
missouri.ag_name: Missouri Attorney General, Consumer Protection Section
missouri.state_note: Missouri's MOSERS runs a defined benefit pension for state employees that vests after five years of service and pays a lifetime monthly benefit.

montana.labor_agency_name: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Employment Standards Division
montana.ag_name: Montana Department of Justice, Office of Consumer Protection
montana.state_note: Montana's Public Employee Retirement Administration (MPERA) runs the state's public employee retirement systems, including defined benefit pensions for state and local workers.

nebraska.labor_agency_name: Nebraska Department of Labor, Office of Labor Standards
nebraska.ag_name: Nebraska Attorney General, Consumer Affairs Response Team
nebraska.state_note: Nebraska's Public Employees Retirement Systems (NPERS) administers six mandatory retirement plans for state, county, school, judges, and State Patrol employees.

nevada.labor_agency_name: Nevada Office of the Labor Commissioner
nevada.ag_name: Nevada Attorney General, Bureau of Consumer Protection
nevada.state_note: Nevada's Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) is a defined benefit plan providing a lifetime base income to qualified state and local public employees.

new hampshire.ag_name: New Hampshire Department of Justice, Consumer Protection and Antitrust Bureau
new hampshire.state_note: The New Hampshire Retirement System (NHRS) is a defined benefit plan paying lifetime pensions to state, county, and municipal employees, teachers, police officers, and firefighters.

new jersey.labor_agency_name: New Jersey Department of Labor & Workforce Development, Division of Wage and Hour Compliance
new jersey.ag_name: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs (Office of the Attorney General)
new jersey.state_note: New Jersey's Division of Pensions & Benefits runs the Public Employees' Retirement System (PERS) and Teachers' Pension and Annuity Fund (TPAF) defined benefit pensions.

new mexico.labor_agency_name: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions — Labor Relations Division
new mexico.ag_name: New Mexico Department of Justice (Office of the Attorney General) — Consumer Protection
new mexico.state_note: New Mexico PERA provides a lifetime defined-benefit pension to public employees, with benefits based on salary and service credit.

new york.labor_agency_name: New York State Department of Labor — Division of Labor Standards
new york.ag_name: New York State Attorney General — Consumer Frauds and Protection Bureau
new york.state_note: New York State and Local Retirement System, run by the State Comptroller, provides pensions to state and local public employees.

north carolina.labor_agency_name: North Carolina Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Bureau
north carolina.ag_name: North Carolina Attorney General — Consumer Protection Division
north carolina.state_note: North Carolina Retirement Systems administers pensions for teachers and state/local public employees; NCDOL notes it does not handle pension plans.

north dakota.labor_agency_name: North Dakota Department of Labor and Human Rights — Wage and Hour Division
north dakota.ag_name: North Dakota Attorney General — Consumer Protection Division
north dakota.state_note: North Dakota PERS provides a defined-benefit hybrid pension to eligible public employees, based on salary, multiplier and service credit.

ohio.labor_agency_name: Ohio Department of Commerce — Bureau of Wage and Hour Administration
ohio.ag_name: Ohio Attorney General — Consumer Protection Section
ohio.state_note: Ohio OPERS provides pension benefits and health coverage to retired public employees, with defined-benefit pensions based on salary and service.

oklahoma.labor_agency_name: Oklahoma Department of Labor — Wage and Hour Unit
oklahoma.ag_name: Oklahoma Attorney General — Consumer Protection Unit
oklahoma.state_note: Oklahoma OPERS is a defined-benefit plan providing lifetime retirement benefits to eligible state and local public employees.

oregon.labor_agency_name: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)
oregon.state_note: Oregon PERS provides a lifetime pension plus an Individual Account Program to most Oregon public-service and state employees.

pennsylvania.labor_agency_name: Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry — Bureau of Labor Law Compliance
pennsylvania.ag_name: Pennsylvania Attorney General — Bureau of Consumer Protection
pennsylvania.state_note: Pennsylvania PSERS administers a defined-benefit pension for public school employees, paying monthly benefits based on salary and service.

rhode island.labor_agency_name: Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training — Labor Standards Unit
rhode island.ag_name: Rhode Island Attorney General — Consumer Protection Unit
rhode island.state_note: Rhode Island ERSRI provides retirement, disability and survivor benefits to state employees, teachers and participating municipal workers.

south carolina.labor_agency_name: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation — Wages and Child Labor Section
south carolina.ag_name: South Carolina Department of Consumer Affairs
south carolina.state_note: South Carolina Retirement System, run by PEBA, is a defined-benefit plan paying a monthly pension to state and local public employees.

south dakota.labor_agency_name: South Dakota Department of Labor and Regulation, Division of Labor Standards and Operational Services (Wage and Hour)
south dakota.ag_name: South Dakota Attorney General, Division of Consumer Protection
south dakota.state_note: South Dakota's public employees get a lifetime pension through the South Dakota Retirement System (SDRS), a defined-benefit plan funded by fixed 6% employee and employer contributions.

tennessee.labor_agency_name: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development, Labor Standards Unit
tennessee.ag_name: Tennessee Attorney General, Division of Consumer Affairs
tennessee.state_note: Tennessee's public workers get a lifetime pension through the Tennessee Consolidated Retirement System (TCRS), which pays lifetime retirement, survivor, and disability benefits after five years of service.

texas.labor_agency_name: Texas Workforce Commission, Wage and Hour Department
texas.ag_name: Texas Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
texas.state_note: Texas state employees get a lifetime monthly pension through the Employees Retirement System of Texas (ERS), based on years of service and highest average salary.

utah.labor_agency_name: Utah Labor Commission, Antidiscrimination and Labor Division, Wage Claim Unit
utah.ag_name: Utah Division of Consumer Protection (Utah Department of Commerce)
utah.state_note: Utah public employees hired since July 2011 choose between a hybrid pension and a 401(k)-style plan through Utah Retirement Systems, with the hybrid paying a monthly benefit for life.

vermont.labor_agency_name: Vermont Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
vermont.ag_name: Vermont Attorney General, Consumer Assistance Program
vermont.state_note: Vermont state employees get a defined-benefit pension through the Vermont State Retirement System, created in 1944, with benefits based on service, age, and final pay and vesting after five years.

virginia.labor_agency_name: Virginia Department of Labor and Industry, Labor and Employment Law Division, Payment of Wage Unit
virginia.ag_name: Virginia Attorney General, Consumer Protection Section
virginia.state_note: Virginia public employees, teachers, and local government workers get a lifetime monthly pension through the Virginia Retirement System (VRS), with membership automatic when hired.

washington.labor_agency_name: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries, Employment Standards Program
washington.ag_name: Washington State Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
washington.state_note: Washington public employees get a lifetime pension through the Department of Retirement Systems (DRS); PERS Plan 2 pays 2% of final pay times years of service after five years.

west virginia.labor_agency_name: West Virginia Division of Labor, Wage and Hour Section
west virginia.ag_name: West Virginia Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
west virginia.state_note: West Virginia public employees get a lifetime pension through the Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), paying 2% of final average salary times years of service, with full benefits at age 60 with five years.

wisconsin.labor_agency_name: Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development, Equal Rights Division, Labor Standards
wisconsin.ag_name: Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection, Bureau of Consumer Protection
wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin public employees get a lifetime pension through the Wisconsin Retirement System (WRS), a fully funded hybrid defined-benefit plan covering state and local workers.

wyoming.labor_agency_name: Wyoming Department of Workforce Services, Labor Standards Division
wyoming.ag_name: Wyoming Attorney General, Consumer Protection and Antitrust Unit
wyoming.state_note: Wyoming public employees are automatically enrolled in a defined-benefit pension through the Wyoming Retirement System (WRS), which pays a guaranteed monthly benefit for life once vested.
